newsitem.title: USA: Gap earnings, sales rise in final quarter.
newsitem.headline: Gap earnings, sales rise in final quarter.

text.p: Popular clothing retailer Gap Inc. posted record fourth quarter profits Thursday in line with Wall Street estimates.
Gap earned $171.2 million, or 62 cents a share compared with $154.6 million, or 54 cents a share for the comparable year-ago period. Sales rose 10 percent to $1.67 billion from $1.52 billion.
Analysts predicted the retailer would earn 62 cents a share, according to First Call.
Gap, which owns Gap, GapKids, Banana Republic and Old Navy stores, said it opened 203 new stores in 1996, and plans to open at least 275 new stores this year.

"Our results demonstrate the strength of our balanced portfolio of apparel brands, with Gap, Banana Republic and Old Navy all improving their profitability in 1996," said Millard S. Drexler, Gap Inc. president and chief executive officer.
Analysts were pleased with the performance.

"They are executing their retail business very effectively and they've had some very appealing merchandise that was attractive and sold at regular prices," said Richard Jaffe, analyst at Schroder Wertheim & Co. "A lot of things came together, the Old Navy business performed well and the apparel was absolutely on target."
Jaffe said the record earnings may be hard to maintain but Gap could grow earnings in the mid-teens range.
Gap's earnings per share have grown at a compound annual rate of 22 percent over the last three years and 21 percent over the last 10 years.
Stacey Pak, an analyst at CS First Boston, also expects earnings will slow.
"The first half of 1996 was so good ... that it's hard to beat that, it's hard to even meet that," she said.
Experts said the company's long term propects are good given Old Navy's strong growth potential in the United States and the possibility of strong international growth for the overall company.
For the year, Gap earned $152.9 million, or $1.60 a share, on sales of $5.28 billion. A year earlier it earned $354.0 million, or $1.23 a share, on sales of $4.39 billion.
Drexler said the company was committed to boosting shareholder value through share repurchase programmes and growth in the core business.
Gap stock fell $1 to $33.25 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Analysts attributed the fall to profit-taking.
